artworks.title: Odysseus Fighting the Beggar Irus
artworks.description: Primaticcio’s Nationalmuseum drawing stages Odyssey XVIII: disguised Odysseus floors Arnaeus — nicknamed Irus — before the jeering suitors. Fontainebleau line keeps the beggar’s challenge as the comic prelude to the bow contest.

artworks.title: Fight between Odysseus and Irus
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum RP-P-1890-A-15578: the palace fistfight that strips Irus of his place at the suitors’ door. Northern print tradition made the Ithacan beggar a stock Odyssey vignette.

films.title: L'Odissea
films.description: Rossi’s Italian-Yugoslav Odyssey keeps the beggar’s bout among the palace episodes — Irus as the bruiser who learns the stranger’s fist.

popCulture.title: Odyssey XVIII (Irus)
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer’s Arnaeus — called Irus for his errands — challenges the beggar Odysseus and is crushed with one blow, the comic bout before the slaughter.
